subject: Hub-and-spoke VPC / intermittent air-gapped telemetry - integration questionnaire
messages:
From: James Olson <james.olson@tethyshealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@tethyshealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-11T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: RFI - hub-and-spoke VPC + intermittent airgap telemetry questions

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for agreeing to take our questionnaire. Tethys is evaluating private deployments where our analytics cluster lives in a central (hub) VPC and multiple hospital sites connect as spokes. Some sites are permanently online; several sites are on a maintenance schedule requiring their spokes to be isolated for up to 48 hours (intermittent air-gapping). We need to understand how Redwood would operate under this model. Below are specific questions — please respond inline where possible and attach any diagrams.

1) Can Redwood run in a hub-only telemetry mode where inference occurs locally in the spoke for critical requests but logs/usage metrics are buffered and uploaded only when the spoke regains connectivity?
2) What components must be reachable during initial model startup and periodic model updates? Can updates be staged via an S3-compatible bucket we control?
3) Describe your KMS/HSM options for private deployments and how key sync/rotation works when spokes are offline for extended windows.
4) What operational controls exist to ensure that telemetry never leaves the spoke unless explicitly permitted (e.g., allowlist by CIDR, signed bundle uploads)?
5) If someone requests an architecture diagram and an operator runbook for on-call recovery (example: model cache corruption post-update), can you provide a sample runbook and escalation matrix?
6) Any constraints we should know about GPU packaging, driver updates, and offline patching?

We prefer concise, bulleted answers and a simple diagram. Also note our procurement team will need an estimated SOW for a three-week pilot (on-prem install + one spoke integration).

Thanks,
James
Senior Infrastructure Architect
Tethys Health Systems

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-11T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFI - hub-and-spoke VPC + intermittent airgap telemetry questions

James — thanks for the clear questions. I've attached a concise network diagram and a short operations appendix that addresses your points. Summary answers below; I'll loop in our infra lead for deeper KMS and patching details.

Quick answers (top-level):
- Yes: Redwood supports a local-first inference mode with buffered telemetry. Our runtime writes metrics to a local encrypted staging area and ships on reconnect; you control the upload policy (time-based, event-triggered, or manual).
- Model updates: initial bootstrap requires access to the control plane to fetch model manifests and signed artifact URLs. After that, models can be staged to an S3-compatible bucket in your VPC; the runtime can be configured to pull from that bucket when connectivity is allowed.
- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS and integration with HSM-backed providers. When spokes are offline, keys remain local; rotation can be configured as coordinated or deferred until reconnect.
- Telemetry controls: allowlist + signed bundles are supported; telemetry collectors can be disabled, and uploads require a signed upload token from the hub (or an operator).
- Runbook + oncall: attached is a sample runbook and escalation matrix (see pilot-sow-draft.docx).
- GPU/patching: we recommend staggered driver updates and provide an offline patch bundle mechanism. Patching is performed with checksums and a dry-run mode.

I'll bring Aditya (serving runtime) and Grace (deployments) into a short internal review to confirm KMS rotation and offline patch mechanics; we should be able to provide a small SOW by end of day tomorrow.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

We need language about transactional model activation vs partial model failures. Also confirm that model manifests are signed and verified locally.

Grace: for KMS, does Redwood require an always-online rotation endpoint for CMK rewrap, or can we operate with deferred rotation and a per-spoke key envelope approach? Also any limitations on driver packaging size for offline bundles?

Aisha / Grace — quick bullets from runtime side:

- Partial artifact downloads: the runtime maintains a staging directory and verifies artifact checksums before swapping into the active model path. If a download is interrupted, we keep the previous model active; the new model activation is atomic. We log a distinct metric for partial/download-failed and expose it via the local admin HTTP endpoint.
- Model manifests: always signed with our artifact signing key; verification happens locally. We can accept your signing chain if you prefer to host manifests in your bucket and sign with your key.
- Staged pull: we support scheduling (cron-like) or operator-triggered pulls. Pull failures generate an alert and increment a backoff counter to avoid DOSing the hub.
- Local inference with metric buffering: metrics are written to an encrypted WAL (append-only) and rotated to compressed signed bundles. Uploads can be gated by operator approval or an allowed CIDR list.

Note: we'll add wording about atomic activation and WAL retention policy to the runbook.

— Aditya
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFI - hub-and-spoke VPC + intermittent airgap telemetry questions

James / Procurement — attaching the technical appendix requested and a draft three-week pilot SOW. Key points (summary):

- Architecture: Redwood runs in a spoke-local mode for inference. Telemetry is buffered in an encrypted WAL and uploaded only when operator policy allows; uploads can be signed bundles or picked from a customer S3 bucket. (See redwood-hub-spoke-networking.pdf)
- Model builds/updates: initial control-plane contact required for manifest integrity checks. After onboarding we can operate fully from your S3-compatible bucket; our runtime will verify signatures before activation.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed CMKs with envelope encryption. Rotation modes: coordinated (preferred) or deferred. For deferred rotation spokes retain local key material and accept new ciphertexts upon reconnect; an operator can trigger rewrap when online.
- Offline patching: we provide a driver/agent bundle signed and checksummed. Patching follows a dry-run, verify, and staged-apply procedure. Bundle size capped at 2GB per spoke to match limited upstream bandwidth — larger bundles possible with extended maintenance windows.
- Runbook: included operator runbook covers common recovery flows: interrupted model pull, corrupted cache, forced rollback, and contact escalation (oncall infra -> solutions lead -> customer success).

Next steps we propose:
1) Pilot kickoff (3 weeks): week 0 prep (access, bucket, firewall allowlist), week 1 install + smoke tests on single spoke, week 2 integrate policy and telemetry gating, week 3 resilience tests and handover.
2) Share minimal procurement contact and preferred dates.
3) We will provide a short SOC2 artifacts checklist as a separate note to Procurement.

If that works, I'll share the SoW and a DoA/engagement email for signatures.

Best regards,
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
